newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Taiwan key to U.S. arms talks.
newsitem.headline: China says Taiwan key to U.S. arms talks.

text.p: China said on Tuesday the key issue for Beijing during arms proliferation talks with the United States was the U.S. sale of weapons to Taiwan.
The U.S. had exported large numbers of advanced weapons to Taiwan and Beijing hoped Washington would pay attention to its concerns, Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told reporters.
The spokesman made the remarks as U.S. Undersecretary of State Lynn Davis was holding talks with Chinese negotiators on a range of arms proliferation issues.
"The most sensitive and important issue is that the United States has violated the August 17 communique by exporting large numbers of advanced weapons to Taiwan," Cui told a regular news briefing.
Under the August 17, 1982 communique, the U.S. pledged to reduce the quality and quantity of arms sales to Taiwan.
"We have repeatedly expressed our view to the U.S. side and hope the U.S. will pay attention to it," Cui said.
